product.tagline: Use your Android phone as a trackpad, keyboard, remote and second screen for your Windows PC, over your own Wi-Fi, with no account or cloud.
product.summary: Portal Remote pairs an Android phone with a Windows PC on the same network and lets you drive the PC from the sofa. Move the cursor and type, watch the screen live, cast to the PC or a TV, and send links and files either way. The phone talks straight to a small tray app on the PC, so there is no account and no relay in between.

features.title: Trackpad, keyboard and remote
features.detail: A precision trackpad with multi-finger gestures and momentum, a keyboard with shortcut keys, media keys, and a TV-style D-pad for the couch.

features.title: See the PC's screen
features.detail: Live mirroring at about 14.5 frames a second, per monitor or a single app's window. Pinch to zoom up to 4x and tap to click where you looked.

features.title: Play and cast
features.detail: See what the PC is playing with cover art and a real scrubber, and send a link or a file to the PC, a Roku or a DLNA TV.

features.title: A browser that blocks ads
features.detail: The in-app browser blocks ads, trackers and popups, turns down cookie prompts from the major consent vendors, and hands any video it finds to the cast button.

features.title: Send things both ways
features.detail: Share from the phone's share sheet or press Ctrl+Alt+V on the PC and it lands on the other device's clipboard. Browse a shared folder on the PC to download or upload.

features.title: Watch the machine
features.detail: A live dashboard of CPU per core, memory, network, every drive and the busiest processes. The PC only measures itself while you are looking.

features.title: An assistant that asks first
features.detail: One conversation shared by phone and PC that can press media keys, type or run shortcuts on the PC, approved one action at a time. Needs Agent Platform, which the app sets up.

features.title: Pairs in one tap
features.detail: Tap the PC in the list the phone finds on your network and allow it on the PC, or scan a QR code. Both halves update themselves from GitHub releases.
